tldr: LLM-Planner is a novel method that uses large language models for few-shot grounded high-level planning for embodied agents, achieving competitive performance on the ALFRED dataset using less than 0.5% of paired training data.
contributions: Proposing LLM-Planner, an LLM-based planner for embodied instruction following that enables few-shot planning without parameter updates
Introducing a dynamic grounded re-planning algorithm that incorporates perceived objects from the environment into prompts to generate physically grounded plans
Demonstrating competitive few-shot performance on ALFRED with less than 0.5% of training data, while existing methods barely complete any task under the same setting
methods: LLM-Planner uses a hierarchical planning approach with an LLM (e.g., GPT-3/TEXT-DAVINCI-003) as a high-level planner that generates sequences of subgoals (HLPs) via in-context learning with a few paired examples. A frozen BERT-base model retrieves the K most similar in-context examples via kNN based on instruction embeddings, and logit biases constrain the output to allowed actions and objects. When the agent gets stuck (fails an action or exceeds a step threshold), a grounded re-planning algorithm re-prompts the LLM with observed objects from the environment to dynamically regenerate the plan. The low-level planner, trained on synthetic simulator data, maps each subgoal to primitive actions independently of the language instruction.
results: On the ALFRED dataset, LLM-Planner achieves competitive performance using less than 0.5% of paired training data, outperforming multiple baselines trained with the full training set. Existing methods can barely complete any task successfully under the same few-shot setting. The method was evaluated by integrating with the perception module and low-level planner from HLSM [3].
limitations: The approach depends on an object detector to perceive objects in the environment for grounded re-planning
Requires a low-level planner to convert high-level plans into primitive actions
Evaluation is conducted on ALFRED, and while the authors claim generalizability to other datasets, extensive validation across diverse environments is not presented
The method uses GPT-3 (TEXT-DAVINCI-003), which may incur high inference costs and latency for real-time embodied applications
